issues.description: Example 7 (USAMO adapted) has a fundamental error: it incorrectly assumes that perpendiculars from feet of perpendiculars always concur at P, leading to a contradiction. This misleads students.
Hard examples are weak: Example 6 is too vague, Example 7 is invalid.

strengths: Excellent coverage of theory, especially edge cases.
Real olympiad problems in Section 1 (BNO 2018, Balkan 2019).
Clear explanation of common mistakes in Section 6.
suggestions: Add one more easy example to meet the 3-example requirement.
Rewrite or replace Example 7 with a valid hard problem from actual olympiads.
Provide a correct proof for Example 5 (orthic triangle) instead of skipping calculations.

math_errors.problem: In Example 7, the article claims: 'The perpendicular from A₁ to BC is PA₁.' This is only true if P lies on the perpendicular to BC at A₁, which isn't generally true. This leads to the false conclusion that perpendiculars always concur.
math_errors.fix: Redesign the example with actual USAMO 2010 Problem 2 or a valid alternative that correctly applies Carnot's theorem.

verdict_reasoning: Score max 5 due to a critical math error in Example 7 (body of article). Structure is mostly good but lacks one easy example. Hard examples need improvement.
